images.title: A high outlier pulls the mean
images.purpose: Show that one very high value pulls the mean to the right of the median.
images.composition: One wide dot plot across the middle of the frame, a cluster of dots on the left and a single dot far to the right, with two small markers under the line.
exact_structure: A dark grey (#2B2B2B) number line from 0 to 40 with small ticks every 5 and numbered ticks at 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40.
7 dots in total, one above each value: 1, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are teal (#0072B2) dots; 40 is a vermilion (#D55E00) dot.
A wide empty gap between the dot at 8 and the dot at 40; the label Outlier sits above the vermilion dot.
Under the line a reddish purple (#CC79A7) triangle points up at 6, labelled Median = 6.
Under the line an amber (#E69F00) triangle points up at 10, labelled Mean = 10, sitting to the right of the median triangle.
rejection: a number of dots other than 7
the mean marker drawn left of the median marker
markers at values other than 6 and 10
images.takeaway: A high outlier lifts the mean above the median, while the median stays with the middle of the data.
images.description: A dot plot of 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 40 with the median marked at 6 and the mean at 10, the 40 dot labelled outlier.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask why the mean sits to the right of most dots, and which single dot is responsible.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the far right dot and the mean marker drift towards it makes the outlier effect clear.
